descriptionChirho: Interrogative adverb asking about location or direction, used in direct and indirect questions ('Where is he?' 'Where are you going?'). Distinctly rendered: Spanish 'donde/a donde', Hindi 'kahaan' (कहाँ), Arabic 'ayna' (أَيْنَ), Korean 'eodie' (어디에/어디로), Swahili 'wapi'. This is the prototypical interrogative spatial sense, consistently distinguished from the indefinite and approximative uses across all target languages.

Indefinite adverb indicating an unspecified location, used when the exact place is unknown or left vague ('somewhere in a certain place'). Distinctly rendered: Spanish 'en algun lugar/en alguna parte', Hindi 'kahiin' (कहीं), Arabic 'fi makaanin' (فِي مَكَانٍ), Korean 'eodieseo/eodingage' (어디에서/어딘가에), Swahili 'mahali fulani'. The shift from interrogative kahaan to indefinite kahiin in Hindi, and from ayna to fi makaanin in Arabic, confirms this as a separate lexical sense.

Adverb of approximation used to indicate an inexact quantity or degree ('about four thousand years'). Distinctly rendered: Spanish 'aproximadamente', Hindi 'lagbhag' (लगभग), Arabic 'taqriiban' (تَقريباً), Korean 'eoneudeot' (어느덧), Swahili 'hivi'. The translations uniformly shift away from spatial vocabulary toward numerical estimation vocabulary, confirming a genuinely different semantic function from the interrogative and indefinite locative senses.
